newsitem.title: GERMANY: German orders data disappoint, but revision seen.
newsitem.headline: German orders data disappoint, but revision seen.

text.p: German industry orders slowed sharply in September, a report said Tuesday, but analysts said it was too early to write off prospects of economic recovery because the data were likely to be revised upwards.
Industrial orders fell by 3.6 percent in September against August, while the August figure was revised down to show a modest gain of 0.1 percent on the previous month.
Economist Holger Schmieding at Merrill Lynch in Frankfurt called the number "disappointing," but echoed a warning by the Economics Ministry that the numbers would be revised up later.
Initial September data are seen as particularly unreliable by economists because companies are usually late in reporting figures after the summer break.

Matthias Haffner of Barclays de Zoete Wedd dismissed a slowdown in export orders as mainly linked to erratic factors. But a tailing off in domestic orders in the third quarter against the second quarter was more worrying, he said.
"We expect an upward revision, but I cannot see that we will end up with a positive number for September," he said.
Most economists agree the German economy should grow by at least 1 percent this year, and forecasts tend to agree with official expectations of 2.5 percent growth in 1997.
But if the setback in orders, which followed the release Monday of weak industrial production figures, is confirmed, then there may be cause to take another look at recovery prospects.
"It is all getting tighter. If there is another bad number next month, then we will have to rethink," Haffner said.
Commerzbank's Peter Pietsch agreed. "This is a very disappointing number and is definitely a dampener on optimistic expectations," he said in an interview.

The industry orders data coincided with the release of the industry-based Federation of German Chambers of Commerce (DIHT) autumn survey of 25,000 companies, which found that businesses expected the recovery to continue.
